correctness.rationale: Fraïssé realization reduces complete singleton types exactly to pairs of a down-set and an up-set satisfying \(L<U\). In a disjoint union of chains, pure types produce twice the product of geometric polynomials minus the single all-incomparable duplicate; mixed types have exactly \(j-1\) choices at grade \(j\) in each chain of length at least \(j\). Degreewise replacement of all unresolved factors by \(S_{j-1}\) changes the coefficient of degree \(j\) by exactly \(q_j\), while the mixed term contributes \((j-1)q_j\), yielding \(c_j=2[z^j]B_j+(j+1)q_j\). Inductively this determines every short-chain multiplicity; \(n\le2\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) allows at most two residual chains, each uniquely determined by remaining total size. Explicit even/odd profiles coincide below the cutoff and differ by \(r+1\) at its boundary. Brute transitivity enumeration matched the closed formula for all 66 profiles through eight vertices; an independent integer-partition census verified exact reconstruction and lower-cutoff sharpness for all 28,628 profiles through 30 vertices. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal result.

value.rationale: This is a natural inverse question for the numerical distribution of finite-base nonalgebraic one-point types in a canonical homogeneous relational structure: how far into the comparability grades must one look before the entire parameter shape is determined? The all-size threshold floor(n/2), unique recovery procedure and explicit matching obstructions show a sharp information boundary, not merely a new normalization or small enumeration. The same-size same-component scalar collision (1,4,12) versus (2,2,13), both 331 types, illustrates why retaining grade is mathematically consequential. The result is restricted to an intrinsically motivated family of bases, but solves the precise inverse problem completely.
